key_insight: HARP reframes LLM-based recommendation as communication between user and item agents, rather than relying only on a static user profile. Its training-free, dual-profile approach organizes this communication into four stages: BUILD, TRANSMIT, UNDERSTAND, and SYNC.
problem_solved: Existing memory-augmented recommenders treat users and items asymmetrically: only users receive structured profiles, profile information must fit into a limited reranker prompt, and profiles remain frozen after warmup.
method: BUILD: Create agent self-descriptions within a dual-profile framework for users and items.
TRANSMIT and UNDERSTAND: Pass profile information along the collaborative graph and interpret the other side.
SYNC: Update profiles using the next interaction instead of leaving them frozen.
impact: HARP offers practitioners a training-free framework for exploring more balanced, adaptive personalization in LLM recommenders. The supplied abstract is truncated, so benchmark gains and efficiency claims cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: static user-only memory versus communicating user and item profiles.

paper_title: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation
paper_authors: Zhen Tao, Xun Zhou, Xuhui Chen, Ziyue Qiao, Qingqiang Sun
